I am a research associate at the [Oden Institute for Computational Engineering and Sciences](https://oden.utexas.edu/) at the University of Texas at Austin. I am also affiliated with [CosmicAI](https://www.cosmicai.org/), the NSF–Simons AI Institute for Cosmic Origins.

My research is in unsupervised learning for scientific data that are large, high-dimensional, and noisy, where no labels exist and the first question is simply what the data contain. I am drawn to this problem because the populations and physical regimes in a data set are there to be found, yet every method brings its own assumptions about what counts as structure, and those assumptions decide what a scientist ends up seeing. My own methods rest on prototype learning, learned connectivity graphs, and low-dimensional embeddings, and I build them so that what they find can be defended as evidence rather than dismissed as an artifact of the analysis.

For the past decade that work has lived inside astronomy: separating the regimes of dense gas in star-forming clouds, tracing the evolutionary phases of the cores that become stars, and building a Bayesian census of young stars from millions of infrared sources. My long-term goal is a general paradigm for physics-informed unsupervised learning.
